beur-hagra/2:_: 462—and that it has none. There it is with water and salt, per Rosh's explanation there:
beur-hagra/3:א: 463—karmel, etc. Rambam; and so Rif explained there: the Tanna taught one may not crush, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ב: And likewise when they crush. There the Tanna taught one may not crush, etc.; Ulla said, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ג: The new ones—for this is called crushing; see Ran there:
beur-hagra/3:ד: But only. There Rava criticized him, etc., per Rif's explanation:
chok-yaakov/1:_: It is allowed to burn two shevals together. And like the 2nd of the 2nd and the tzal Plogta Dabei and Raba in the P. every hour and KIL Karba Deshri Akal and K.K. the Rif and the Rash but it is a bit difficult the source stated in the issue of page M. AA concludes there Dhaddar Biya Abei and thanks the Rabbi Dakh13 Sheri Damia Midev Daev Kahg and Amsamsai' and not Peligi but in the kidneys that were dried while in the pot and KIL Karba Deshri, even in the 23rd and 23rd of siman 11, they rule to write the Hai Gebba Dakh13 Sheri, and in truth in siman 19 I did not write, only the last phrase and the last verse:
chok-yaakov/2:א: And that it should not have water. Even though salt also chametzs as in siman 462, nevertheless it is different here because it is nullified as minimal—Ran:
chok-yaakov/2:ב: This too is forbidden. But regarding roasting sheaves above, which is permitted—even for us, since it is only a mere concern, and even in the pot it is permitted, as Tosafos Menachot 54 wrote:
chok-yaakov/3:_: Lest it was not roasted well in fire. Specifically in karmel the Rambam is concerned; but in roasted flour the Rambam ruled in ch. 5 permitting cooking l'chatchila; possibly also Rashi's view 40b where Rava criticized the pot with roasted onion flour—Tosafos resolve the difficulty there. However the Mechaber concluded only baked matzah, implying roasted is forbidden in every case per Tosafos; so Beit Yosef in siman 461 citing Rabbeinu Yerucham—even though Rambam also wrote like the Mechaber only baked matzah, nevertheless he wrote in explanation that roasted flour is permitted unlike the Mechaber's wording. See Magen Avraham: requires study if placed b'dieved in food whether they forbid from this concern, for Rashi permits l'chatchila, and Beit Yosef cites Rambam; difference regarding matzah kneaded with flour and baked then placed in dish—one should be stringent with matzah since it separates flour from fire—end. From his wording it seems even in roasted karmel Rambam and Rashi permit l'chatchila—certainly not, for the Gemara implies forbidding and Rambam in explanation forbids—so it is a d'oraisa doubt and forbidden b'dieved; but in roasted flour since they permit l'chatchila one may rely b'dieved for benefit or until after Passover—it appears to me:
peri-megadim/1:_: From oil—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham (1) also brought Ran's view; from 462 (3) honey should be wine; in (6) in honey water more forbidden—distinction between mixed long before Passover water turned to fruit juice versus mixed any water in fruit juice immediately—see Ohel Moshe responsa 122 and Peri Chadash; Taz 465 on this. However Magen Avraham there letter (6) distinguishes fermenting and later fermenting—so Peri Chadash. For practical law do not be lenient to eat except minimal water nullified in sixty and later fermentation like that case 462 (3); possibly even without long time permitted if not changed—even minimal water and long time do not be lenient unless great need—one may argue. Water-honey drink where water is primary—forbid and leave or benefit; the lenient in great need do not act arrogantly as Magen Avraham (6) at length:
peri-megadim/2:_: Forbidden—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham in 462 (4): reason we do not knead with fruit juice lest little water mixed; here not that reason; but concern for Rashi's view fruit juice alone is hardened; even oil Chafetz Chayim without salt is hardened; nevertheless seif 1 not to act by hand, only concern moisture b'dieved no concern—and siman 445 Taz (3); and if so there (8) will be explained; and per view fruit juice with water burn immediately—say Menachot and Rambam ch. 5; and see Magen Avraham (8) from this:
peri-megadim/3:_: But only—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham Pesachim 40b (2) see there; Taz wrote Tur properly challenged—for practical law no dispute between crushed and baked, only where workers common forbidden and Rava at his place workers uncommon. What he wrote lentils—possibly where spreading workers common—all agree lentil flour forbidden to cook even for those permitting baked matzah; see Tur; Rif and R' Avraham Avinu; Rosh wrote plainly baked matzah; Rif explained chasis baked matzah; Rosh explained lentil flour like eruv. For us forbidden legume flour—see 453; lentil flour if fell in food perhaps like whole legumes if majority permitted food—453. Some do not eat baked matzah except last Yom Tov day—fear confusion or unbaked flour inside; soaking cold ground matzah—one reason no prohibition, second reason perhaps—and world relies on Mechaber and cooks baked matzah; Rabbenu Yerucham silent so Peri Chadash; Magen Avraham (5) and (8) will explain more:
